stops.note: Portuguese auto 'act, ceremony' (from Latin actus) plus da fé 'of the faith'; the Portuguese Inquisition, founded in 1536, held its first public auto da fé in Lisbon in 1540, where sentences were read before the condemned were handed to civil authorities for execution
Voltaire's Candide (1759), set partly in Lisbon, satirises an auto-da-fé staged to prevent further earthquakes after the 1755 disaster

current_meaning: the burning of a heretic by the Inquisition; any public burning of condemned things
